final_answer:
A distributive law between two copies is determined by the relation
\[
x_jx_i=a_{ji}+q_{ji}x_ix_j,\qquad x_i^2=x_j^2=0,
\]
where associativity forces
\[
q_{ji}\ne0,\qquad a_{ji}(1+q_{ji})=0.
\]
Thus either \(a_{ji}=0\), or \(q_{ji}=-1\).

The pair algebra is simple exactly when \(a_{ji}\ne0\). In that case
\[
x_jx_i+x_ix_j=a_{ji},
\]
and after rescaling it is \(M_2(k)\). If \(a_{ji}=0\), the ideal generated by \(x_i\) is a nonzero proper ideal.

For a triple \(i<j<\ell\), comparing the two reductions of \(x_\ell x_jx_i\) gives
\[
a_{ji}(q_{\ell j}q_{\ell i}-1)=0,\qquad
a_{\ell j}(1-q_{ji}q_{\ell i})=0,\qquad
a_{\ell i}(q_{\ell j}-q_{ji})=0.
\]
If all six pairs are simple, then all \(q_{ji}=-1\), and these conditions are automatically satisfied. Hence
\[
S_p=6.
\]

For such maximizers the total algebra is generated by \(x_1,\dots,x_4\) with
\[
x_i^2=0,\qquad x_jx_i+x_ix_j=a_{ji}\ne0.
\]
This is the Clifford algebra of the symmetric bilinear form with matrix
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}
0&a&b&c\\
a&0&d&e\\
b&d&0&f\\
c&e&f&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
It is simple exactly when \(B\) is nondegenerate. Its determinant is
\[
(af)^2+(be)^2+(cd)^2-2afbe-2afcd-2becd.
\]
Let
\[
X=af,\qquad Y=be,\qquad Z=cd.
\]
For each \((X,Y,Z)\in(k^\times)^3\), there are \((p-1)^3\) choices of \((a,b,c,d,e,f)\).

The zero determinant condition becomes
\[
X^2+Y^2+Z^2-2XY-2XZ-2YZ=0.
\]
Scaling by \(Z\), the number of solutions in \((k^\times)^3\) is
\[
(p-1)(p-2).
\]
Therefore the number of nondegenerate choices is
\[
(p-1)^3-(p-1)(p-2)=(p-1)(p^2-3p+3).
\]
Thus
\[
K_p=(p-1)^3\cdot (p-1)(p^2-3p+3)
=(p-1)^4(p^2-3p+3).
\]
Since this is positive for every odd prime \(p\), we also have
\[
T_p=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{(S_p,T_p,K_p)=\left(6,\ 1,\ (p-1)^4(p^2-3p+3)\right)}.
\]
